questions.stem: A force of 50 N pushes a box 4 m along a floor. How much work is done?
questions.explanation: Work done = force x distance = 50 x 4 = 200 J. Option A divides instead of multiplying. Option C adds the values. Option D gives the wrong unit: work is measured in joules (J), not newtons (N).

questions.stem: A student holds a heavy bag motionless above their head. How much work is being done on the bag?

options.text: A large amount, because the bag is heavy
It depends on how long they hold it
Zero, because the bag is not moving
Equal to the weight of the bag

questions.explanation: Work done = force x distance moved in the direction of the force. Since the bag is stationary (distance = 0), no work is done on the bag, regardless of how heavy it is or how long it is held. The student's muscles are using chemical energy to maintain the position, but no mechanical work is done on the bag.

questions.stem: A crane lifts a 200 kg steel beam 15 m vertically. How much work does the crane do against gravity? (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: The force needed to lift the beam equals its weight = mg = 200 x 10 = 2000 N. Work done = force x distance = 2000 x 15 = 30 000 J. This work done equals the gravitational potential energy gained. Option A uses mass instead of weight. Option D multiplies by an extra factor.

questions.stem: A friction force of 30 N acts on a sliding object that moves 5 m. What happens to the 150 J of work done against friction?

options.text: It is transferred to the kinetic energy store of the object
It is transferred to the thermal energy stores of the surfaces
It is transferred to the gravitational potential energy store

questions.explanation: Work done against friction = 30 x 5 = 150 J. This energy is transferred to the thermal energy stores of the rubbing surfaces, causing them to heat up. Energy cannot be destroyed (conservation of energy). Friction removes kinetic energy from the object rather than adding to it. The object stays at the same height, so GPE is unchanged.

questions.stem: A person pushes a 800 N shopping trolley 20 m across a car park using a horizontal force of 40 N. How much work does the person do?
questions.explanation: Work done = force x distance in the direction of force = 40 x 20 = 800 J. A common error is using the weight (800 N) instead of the pushing force (40 N), which would give 16 000 J. The weight acts vertically, but the trolley moves horizontally, so the weight does no work in the horizontal direction.
